newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh taka loses early edge on dlr demand.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh taka loses early edge on dlr demand.

text.p: The Bangladesh taka lost its early edge to close flat at 44.2100/2200 to the dollar in interbank trading on Wednesday amid demands for the U.S. currency from importers.
Dealers said the local currency slipped immediately after opening at 43.2000/2100 per dollar level.
"Dollar demand suddenly rose when importers who couldn't buy on Tuesday returned," said one dealer.
Tight selling by the state-owned banks also helped the dollar.
The call money rates closed at 8.0 to 8.5 from previous at 8.0 to 9.0 percent.
